picks.file: Kaart met stadsplattegrond van Leiden en omgeving, ingekleurd (1574).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view of the walled town and its surroundings, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 2
picks.why: clean colored single sheet; town drawn with its houses inside the walls; trimmed toward the town, cartouche and outer countryside cut

picks.file: Gezicht op Leiden Leyden (titel op object), RP-P-AO-10-18L.jpg
picks.what: Profile view of the city, engraving in Merian’s Topographia Germaniae Inferioris
picks.why: general view with the Pieterskerk, Hooglandse Kerk and town hall tower; firmly dated (Wüthrich NLB 97); sheet margins cut

picks.file: Gezicht op de Hooglandse Kerk in Leiden De Hogelandsche Kerk - Eglise de Hogeland (titel op object), RP-P-1905-1020.jpg
picks.who: J.B. Clermans, printed by Desguerrois & Co.
picks.why: only usable view for this period; one of the city’s main churches; trimmed to the image, captions cut

picks.what: The town hall on the Breestraat, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the city’s best-known facade before the 1929 fire; cleaner copy of #25; caption strip cut

picks.file: Leiden in vogelvlucht, Objectnr PV KRET70.jpg
picks.what: View over the roofs along the Breestraat, photograph (Erfgoed Leiden)
picks.why: dated 5 June 1927, probably taken from the town hall tower; old town and a main church

picks.what: Canal in the historic center, photograph
picks.why: sharp wide canal view with gabled houses; best modern general view among the candidates

gaps: P0: no real candidates (#1 is a 19th-century drawing misdated from its shelfmark)
notes: P1: B&H Leiden is in vol. 2 (1575); the cartouche itself is dated 1574. P2: #12 (Doesburg after Blaeu) is a finer view but undated — ‘1723’ comes from the object number; #15 is a Blaeu profile with only the printer’s death year. P3: Rapenburg facade rows of 1807 (#19–21) are elevations, not views. P6: no skyline photo; Burcht photos (#36–38) are single-structure close-ups.
